title: Social modulation of chronic pelvic pain: Neural inter-individual co-variation and partner interaction
summary:
Pain is not only a physical sensation; it is also influenced by the people around us. Support from a loved one can make short‑lasting pain feel less intense and improve mood. For people with long‑lasting pain, however, a very caring partner can sometimes have the opposite effect and make pain feel worse.
This project looks at couples in which the woman has endometriosis and chronic pelvic pain. The study will scan both partners’ brains at the same time to see how their brains “work together” when the partner tries to support the woman during pain. It will then follow the couple in everyday life with brief phone or app questions to find out how daily partner behavior and pain levels are linked. The aim is to understand how supportive behavior from a partner can help or, in some situations, unintentionally worsen pain, so that better support strategies can be developed for couples living with endometriosis.

interventions.name:
Hyperscanning fMRI in 75 couples 
We will conduct hyperscanning fMRI in 75 romantic couples, including 25 healthy control couples and 50 couples in which the female partner has endometriosis. Using simultaneous fMRI, we will investigate (a) individual neural responses and (b) brain-to-brain couplin

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Age 18 – 45 years 
• Subjects with the ability to follow study instructions and likely to attend and complete all required visits 
• Written informed consent of the participant 
• Willingness of the participant to receive SMS to their own smartphones and fill out short questionnaires using the provided link
• Being committed to an ongoing romantic relationship and living as a couple for at least 6 months 
• Subjects are able to speak, write and understand the German language sufficiently well (at the investigators discretion) to complete all required study procedures 

Additional inclusion criteria for patients: 
• Impairment due to chronic pelvic pain due to endometriosis
Exclusion criteria:
For all participants: 
• Withdrawal of participant consent (defined as a study participant who explicitly takes back his or her consent) 
• Standard MRI exclusion criteria (e.g., pregnancy, claustrophobia, pacemaker, artificial heart valves, cochlear implants, vessel clips, metal implants, prior brain surgery, permanent make-up, large scale tattoos on head or nape of the neck) 
• Current alcohol or drug dependence (F10.2-F19.2) 

Additional exclusion criteria for healthy controls:
• Presence of a psychiatric disorder according to DSM-5, confirmed by Mini-International Neuropsychiatric Interview (Mini-DIPS) at V1. 
• Self-reported family history of any psychiatric disorder.
